official_measurement_examples.name: Schedule 1 gate
official_measurement_examples.fact: Under the 2017 town and country planning EIA regime, Schedule 1 development requires EIA; that classification is distinct from whether planning permission is ultimately granted.

official_measurement_examples.name: Schedule 2 screening gate
official_measurement_examples.fact: Schedule 2 development meeting criteria or located in sensitive areas can require screening for likely significant effects; crossing an indicative threshold is not itself the final EIA or planning outcome.

official_measurement_examples.name: Threshold caution
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance says it should not be presumed that development above indicative thresholds always needs EIA or that development below them can never have significant effects.

official_measurement_examples.name: Scoping distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A scoping opinion concerns the scope and level of detail of environmental information; it is not a development consent or planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Environmental Statement role
official_measurement_examples.fact: An Environmental Statement supplies environmental information for decision-making and does not itself grant permission or prove impacts are acceptable.

official_measurement_examples.name: EOR transition status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The March 2026 Environmental Outcomes Reports material is a reform roadmap and government response; it must not be treated as if it has already displaced the operative EIA/SEA legal requirements for a current case.

official_measurement_examples.name: SEA distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Strategic Environmental Assessment applies to qualifying plans and programmes and is distinct from project-level Environmental Impact Assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Regime separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Town and country planning EIA, infrastructure planning EIA, forestry EIA and other sector regimes have separate legal scopes and must not be silently merged.

core_rules: EIA screening opinion is not planning permission
a negative screening opinion is not general environmental clearance
a positive screening opinion is not automatic refusal
Schedule 1 EIA requirement does not predetermine planning outcome
Schedule 2 thresholds are screening criteria not parcel scoring cutoffs
scoping opinion is not development consent
Environmental Statement submission is not permission
SEA for plans is distinct from project-level EIA
sector-specific EIA regimes must retain legal scope
Environmental Outcomes Reports reform documents must not be treated as already replacing operative EIA law
mitigation considered at screening must retain the exact measures and uncertainty context
sensitive-area status must not be reduced to a universal distance rule
EIA evidence does not determine ownership access or utility capacity
environmental assessment does not reserve development capacity
no parcel EIA clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
